name: Geography
topics: The earth and the solar system
Landforms: mountains, plateaus, plains and their formation
Rivers, coasts, deserts and other landforms
Map reading: scale, distance, direction and relief described in words

questions.q: Which of the following planets in the solar system is closest to the Sun?
questions.e: Mercury is the planet closest to the Sun, at about 58 million km away. Venus, Earth and Mars are progressively farther out in that order.
questions.p: Mercury na di planet wey close pass to Sun, e dey like 58 million km comot. Venus, Earth and Mars dey far pass am.

questions.q: Which term best describes the actual shape of the Earth?
questions.e: The Earth is not a perfect sphere; it bulges slightly at the equator and is flattened at the poles due to its rotation. This shape is called an oblate spheroid or geoid.
questions.p: Earth no be perfect ball; e dey bulge small for equator and flat for poles because of how e dey turn. Dem dey call dis shape oblate spheroid or geoid.

questions.q: The daily alternation of day and night on Earth is mainly caused by which of the following?
o: The elliptical shape of its orbit
questions.e: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis in about 24 hours. The side facing the Sun experiences daytime while the opposite side experiences night.
questions.p: Earth dey do one full turn for im axis for like 24 hours. Di side wey face sun go get daytime while di oda side go get night.

questions.q: Town P is located on longitude 15°W while Town Q is located on longitude 45°E. If the local time at Town P is 9:00 am, what is the local time at Town Q?
questions.e: Longitude difference = 45° - (-15°) = 60°. Time difference = 60/15 = 4 hours. Since Town Q is east of Town P, its local time is ahead: 9:00 am + 4 hours = 1:00 pm.
questions.p: Longitude difference na 45 minus negative 15 wey be 60°. Time difference na 60/15 = 4 hours. Since Q dey east pass P, im time dey ahead: 9:00am add 4 hours give 1:00pm.

questions.q: Two towns, R and S, lie on the same longitude. Town R is on latitude 6°N while Town S is on latitude 14°N. If 1° of latitude along a meridian equals 111 km, what is the distance between the two towns?
questions.e: Distance along a meridian = difference in latitude x 111 km = (14° - 6°) x 111 km = 8 x 111 = 888 km.
questions.p: Distance for meridian na latitude difference times 111 km = (14-6) x 111 = 8 x 111 = 888 km.

questions.q: The tilt of the Earth's axis at about 23.5° to the vertical, combined with the Earth's revolution around the Sun, is mainly responsible for which of the following?
o: The difference in local time between places
The variation of seasons on Earth
questions.e: Because the Earth's axis is tilted, different parts of the Earth receive more or less direct sunlight at different times of the year as it revolves around the Sun. This produces the seasons.
questions.p: Because Earth axis dey tilt, different parts of Earth go dey receive sunlight differently as e dey waka round Sun. Na so seasons dey happen.

questions.q: Using the Earth's radius as 6400 km and pi = 22/7, calculate the distance along the parallel of latitude 60°N between two towns whose longitudes are 10°E and 40°E.
questions.e: The circumference of the parallel at 60°N = 2 x pi x R x cos60° = 2 x 22/7 x 6400 x 0.5 ≈ 20114 km. The longitude difference is 30°, so the distance = (30/360) x 20114 ≈ 1676 km.
questions.p: Di circumference for di 60°N parallel na 2 x pi x R x cos60° = 2 x 22/7 x 6400 x 0.5 wey be like 20114 km. Longitude difference na 30°, so distance na (30/360) x 20114 wey be like 1676 km.

questions.q: The imaginary lines on a globe that run from the North Pole to the South Pole, and are used to measure distance east or west of Greenwich, are called:
questions.e: Lines that join the North Pole to the South Pole are called meridians of longitude. Lines of latitude, on the other hand, run parallel to the Equator from east to west.
questions.p: Dem lines wey join North Pole to South Pole na meridians of longitude. Latitude lines na the ones wey dey run parallel to Equator for east-west direction.

questions.q: If it is 12:00 noon at the Greenwich Meridian (0°), what is the local time at a town located on longitude 45°E?
questions.e: Every 15° of longitude equals 1 hour of time. 45°E divided by 15 gives 3 hours, and since the town is east of Greenwich, its time is ahead: 12 noon + 3 hours = 3:00pm.
questions.p: Every 15° longitude na 1 hour. 45°E divide by 15 na 3 hours, and since the town dey east of Greenwich, im time dey ahead: 12 noon add 3 hours give 3:00pm.

questions.q: A ship sails from Port Alpha, located on longitude 20°W, to Port Beta, located on longitude 10°E. If the local time at Port Alpha is 6:00am, what is the local time at Port Beta at that same instant?
questions.e: Longitude difference = 10 - (-20) = 30°. Time difference = 30/15 = 2 hours. Port Beta is east of Port Alpha, so its time is ahead: 6:00am + 2 hours = 8:00am.
questions.p: Longitude difference na 10-(-20)=30°. Time difference na 30/15=2 hours. Port Beta dey east pass Port Alpha, so im time dey ahead: 6am add 2 hours give 8am.

questions.q: Two towns lie on latitude 60°N and are 60° of longitude apart. Using the formula Distance = (difference in longitude/360) x 2 x pi x R x cos(latitude), with R = 6,400km, pi = 22/7, and cos 60° = 1/2, calculate the distance between the two towns along that parallel.
questions.e: Distance = (60/360) x 2 x (22/7) x 6400 x 0.5. Working this out: (1/6) x (44/7) x 6400 x 0.5 is approximately 3,352km.
questions.p: Distance = (60/360) x 2 x (22/7) x 6400 x 0.5. If you calculate am well, e go give you about 3,352km.

questions.q: Town Kano-X is located on longitude 45°E, while town Zed is located on longitude 135°W. What is the time difference between the two towns?
questions.e: The two longitudes are exactly 180° apart (45 + 135 = 180), which is the maximum possible longitude separation between any two points on Earth. Time difference = 180/15 = 12 hours, the greatest time difference possible.
questions.p: The two longitudes dey exactly 180° apart (45+135=180), na the biggest separation wey two points fit get for Earth. Time difference na 180/15=12 hours, na im be the highest time difference wey fit dey.

questions.q: Which of the following rocks is formed when molten magma or lava cools and solidifies, either beneath or on the earth's surface?
questions.e: Igneous rocks are formed directly from the cooling and solidification of magma (below the surface) or lava (on the surface). Examples include granite and basalt. Sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are formed by different processes.
questions.p: Igneous rock na di one wey come from magma or lava wey cool down turn solid. Granite and basalt na correct example. Sedimentary and metamorphic rocks get different formation process entirely.

questions.q: Which of these rocks is a common example of a sedimentary rock formed mainly from the compacted remains of marine organisms and calcium-rich deposits?
questions.e: Limestone is a sedimentary rock formed mainly from compacted shells, coral and calcium carbonate deposits in water. Granite is igneous, while marble and gneiss are metamorphic rocks.
questions.p: Limestone na sedimentary rock wey dey form from shell, coral and calcium carbonate wey dey pack together for water. Granite na igneous rock, while marble and gneiss na metamorphic rocks.

questions.q: Marble, which is widely used for flooring and sculpture, is produced when limestone undergoes which process?
o: Rapid cooling of molten rock at the surface
Compaction of sand and shell particles only
Metamorphism involving intense heat and pressure
questions.e: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed when limestone is subjected to great heat and pressure deep within the earth's crust, causing recrystallization of the calcite minerals. This is different from simple compaction or magma cooling.
questions.p: Marble na metamorphic rock wey dey form when limestone meet plenty heat and pressure for inside earth, make di calcite minerals recrystallize. E no be simple compaction or magma wey cool down.

questions.q: The rock cycle shows how rocks change from one type to another over geological time. Which sequence correctly shows an igneous rock being weathered into sediments, then compacted into a new rock type, and finally altered by heat and pressure into another rock type?
o: Metamorphic rock changes to sedimentary rock, then to igneous rock
Igneous rock changes to sedimentary rock, then to metamorphic rock
Sedimentary rock changes to igneous rock, then to metamorphic rock
Igneous rock changes to metamorphic rock, then to sedimentary rock
questions.e: In the rock cycle, igneous rock can weather and erode into sediments, which are compacted into sedimentary rock; this sedimentary rock can later be subjected to heat and pressure to form metamorphic rock. This is the correct natural order described in the question.
questions.p: For rock cycle, igneous rock fit weather turn sediment, dat sediment go press together become sedimentary rock; later heat and pressure fit change am to metamorphic rock. Na dis order di question dey yan about.

questions.q: Which mineral has historically been the major reason for large-scale mining activities on the Jos Plateau in Nigeria?
questions.e: The Jos Plateau in Nigeria is well known historically for large deposits of tin ore (cassiterite), which attracted major mining activities from the colonial era onwards. Coal is mainly associated with Enugu, not Jos.
questions.p: Jos Plateau for Nigeria popular well-well for tin ore (cassiterite) wey dem dey mine since colonial time. Coal na Enugu area dem dey find am pass, no be Jos.

questions.q: A student examined a rock sample and noted these features: it is very hard, has tightly interlocking crystals, shows no visible layering, and it fizzes (releases gas bubbles) when a few drops of dilute acid are placed on it. Which rock is this sample most likely to be?
questions.e: Marble is made of calcite, which reacts with dilute acid to release carbon dioxide gas (fizzing). Its interlocking crystal texture with no layering comes from metamorphism of limestone, unlike granite (igneous, no fizz) or shale/sandstone (sedimentary, usually layered).
questions.p: Marble get calcite wey dey react with acid make e fizz (release gas). Di interlocking crystal and no layering show say na metamorphism happen to limestone turn marble, unlike granite wey no dey fizz or shale/sandstone wey get layers.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a plateau as a landform?
o: A steep-sided landform rising to a sharp peak
A narrow strip of land between two mountain ranges
A large flat lowland area close to sea level
An extensive area of relatively high land with a fairly flat top
questions.e: A plateau is an elevated landform with a relatively flat top, distinguishing it from lowlands (plains) and pointed mountain peaks. It is usually higher than the surrounding land.
questions.p: Plateau na big area wey high well-well but e get flat top. E different from plain wey low, and e different from mountain peak wey sharp.

questions.q: Fold mountains, such as the Atlas Mountains in North Africa, are mainly formed as a result of:
o: the compression and buckling of rock layers due to collision of tectonic plates
the gradual wearing away of soft rocks leaving hard rocks standing
the cooling and solidification of molten rock on the earth's surface
the deposition of sediments by rivers over a long period
questions.e: Fold mountains form when two tectonic plates collide and push against each other, causing rock layers to compress, buckle and fold upward. This is the main process that formed ranges like the Atlas and Alps.
questions.p: Fold mountain dey form when two tectonic plates knock each other, make the rock layers press together, bend and rise up. Na dis process form mountains like Atlas.

questions.q: Block mountains (horsts) are formed when:
o: wind and water erode soft rock, leaving hard rock exposed
volcanic ash and lava accumulate in layers over a long time
magma pushes up the earth's crust without breaking through the surface
two parallel faults occur and the land between them is uplifted while the surrounding land subsides
questions.e: Block mountains form through faulting, where two parallel faults develop and the block of land between them is pushed up (or the surrounding land sinks down), leaving a raised, flat-topped block with steep sides.
questions.p: Block mountain dey form through faulting - two parallel cracks (faults) go appear, and the land wey dey between dem go rise up (or the side land go sink), leave one raised block wit steep side.

questions.q: The Jos Plateau in Nigeria is a good example of a landform mainly associated with:
o: faulting that caused the land to subside sharply
volcanic activity followed by erosion of the surrounding land
deposition of river sediments over millions of years
questions.e: The Jos Plateau was built up by ancient volcanic and igneous activity (the Younger Granite complex), and over time the softer surrounding lowlands were eroded away, leaving the plateau standing above them.
questions.p: Jos Plateau come from old volcanic and rock activity (Younger Granite), and as time dey go, erosion chop the softer land around am, leave the plateau standing high.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a plain from a plateau?
o: A plain is generally low-lying with gentle relief while a plateau is an elevated area with a relatively flat top
A plain is formed only by volcanic activity while a plateau is formed only by erosion
A plain has a flat top and steep sides while a plateau is always low-lying
A plain is always found along the coast while a plateau is found only inland
questions.e: A plain is a low-lying stretch of land with gentle slopes, while a plateau is raised well above sea level but still has a flat surface on top. Both can be formed by different processes, so options about origin or location being fixed are wrong.
questions.p: Plain na low land wey no get plenty slope, but plateau na high land wey still get flat top. The two fit form different ways and no dey tied to only coast or only inland.

questions.q: A geography teacher described a landform to her class: 'This landform appears as an isolated upland area that has survived long periods of weathering and erosion while the land around it was worn down to a much lower level.' This description best fits:
questions.e: A residual mountain is left standing after long weathering and erosion have removed softer surrounding rocks, leaving harder, more resistant rock as an isolated upland. Fold, block and volcanic mountains are formed by folding, faulting or volcanic eruption, not by this kind of differential erosion.
questions.p: Residual mountain na the hard rock wey remain standing after erosion don chop the softer land wey dey surround am for many years. Fold, block and volcanic mountain no dey form like dat - dem come from folding, faulting or eruption.

questions.q: A certain plain along the lower course of the River Niger is formed mainly from silt, sand and clay deposited by the river whenever it overflows its banks during flooding. This type of plain is best classified as:
questions.e: A flood plain (also called an alluvial plain) is formed when a river deposits silt, sand and clay on its banks during floods. A lava plain comes from volcanic flows, a peneplain from long erosion of highlands, and a structural plain from the original rock layout, not river deposition.
questions.p: Flood plain (alluvial plain) na im dey form when river dey drop silt, sand and clay for the bank anytime e flood. Lava plain na from volcano, peneplain na from plenty erosion for high land, structural plain na from how the rock layers dey arrange - none of dem be river deposit like dis one.

questions.q: In the study of rivers, the point where a river begins its journey, usually in highlands or hills, is called the river's:
questions.e: The source is where a river starts, often from a spring, melting snow or hill slope. The mouth is where it ends, while a watershed is the boundary separating river basins.
questions.p: Di source na where river dey start from, like for hill or spring. Mouth na where e dey enter sea, so dem no be di same thing.

questions.q: A long, low ridge of sand and shingle built by waves and currents across the entrance of a bay, often trapping water behind it to form a lagoon, is known as a:
questions.e: A bar is a depositional ridge that stretches completely across a bay, cutting it off from the open sea and often creating a lagoon behind it. A spit is similar but only partly closes the bay, leaving one end open.
questions.p: Bar na sand ridge wey block di whole mouth of bay, e fit make lagoon form behind am. Spit no close am well well, na only part e dey block.

questions.q: A river valley that is deep, narrow and V-shaped, with steep sides, rapids and waterfalls but no floodplain, best represents which stage of river development?
questions.e: In the youthful stage, the river has strong vertical erosion power, cutting deep V-shaped valleys with rapids and waterfalls. Floodplains and meanders only develop later, in the mature and old stages.
questions.p: For youthful stage, river dey cut down strong strong, e dey make deep V-shape valley wit waterfall and rapids. Floodplain and meander go come later for mature and old stage.

questions.q: A crescent-shaped sand dune found in hot deserts, with its horns pointing in the direction the wind is blowing towards, and formed where sand supply is limited, is called a:
questions.e: A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune with horns pointing downwind, formed by wind action where sand is scarce and the surface is fairly flat. A seif dune is long and ridge-like, a yardang is a wind-eroded rock ridge, and a wadi is a dry desert valley.
questions.p: Barchan na crescent shape sand dune wey im horns dey point to where wind dey blow go. E dey form where sand no too plenty. Seif dune be long ridge, yardang na rock wey wind carve, wadi na dry valley.

questions.q: At the mouth of a river, sediments carried downstream are deposited in the sea or lake, building up a low, flat, fan-shaped area of new land often cut by several distributary channels. This landform is called a:
questions.e: A delta forms at a river mouth where the river loses speed on entering a standing water body and drops its load of sediment, building new land split by distributaries. A floodplain forms along the river's middle and lower course, while a levee is a raised bank beside the channel.
questions.p: Delta dey form for river mouth, where river slow down as e enter sea and e drop di sand wey e carry, dat one build new land wey distributary dey cut across. Floodplain na for di river body, levee na raised bank for river side.

questions.q: A meander loop becomes so tightly curved that the narrow neck of land between two bends is eventually broken through by the river during a flood, straightening the main channel. The abandoned loop is later sealed off at both ends by silt deposits, leaving a crescent-shaped body of standing water. What is this water body called?
questions.e: An oxbow lake forms exactly this way: a cut-off meander loop that is sealed off from the main river channel by deposition, leaving a curved, still lake. A crater lake forms in a volcanic crater, and a lagoon forms behind a coastal bar, so they are not formed by river meanders.
questions.p: Oxbow lake na when meander loop cut off from di main river channel, den silt close di two ends make crescent lake remain. Crater lake dey form inside volcano crater, lagoon dey form behind coastal bar, so na river meander cause oxbow lake, no be dem.

questions.q: Which of the following instruments is used to measure the amount of rainfall received in a given area?
questions.e: A rain gauge is a container marked with a scale that collects and measures the amount of rain that falls over a period of time. It is the standard instrument used in weather stations for this purpose.
questions.p: Rain gauge na the gadget wey dem dey use measure how much rain fall for one place. Na im be the correct answer because na im work be to collect rain water.

questions.q: Which instrument is used by meteorologists to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.e: A barometer measures the pressure exerted by the atmosphere. Changes in this pressure help in predicting weather conditions such as rain or clear skies.
questions.p: Barometer na the instrument wey dem dey use measure air pressure. E dey help predict if rain go fall or if weather go clear.

questions.q: On a particular day in Sokoto, the highest temperature recorded was 38°C and the lowest was 22°C. What was the diurnal range of temperature for that day?
questions.e: Diurnal range of temperature is the difference between the highest and lowest temperature recorded in a day. Here, 38°C minus 22°C gives 16°C.
questions.p: Diurnal range na the difference between the highest and lowest temperature for one day. 38°C minus 22°C na 16°C, so C na correct answer.

questions.q: In a standard weather station, instruments like the dry-bulb and wet-bulb thermometers are kept inside a wooden box called the Stevenson screen. What is the main purpose of this screen?
o: To record the amount of sunshine hours
To measure the direction wind blows from
To protect the instruments from direct sunlight and rain while allowing free air circulation
questions.e: The Stevenson screen is a louvered wooden box that shields thermometers and other instruments from direct sunlight, rain and strong winds, while its slatted sides allow air to flow freely so that accurate readings of air temperature can be taken.
questions.p: Stevenson screen na wooden box wey get small holes for side, e dey protect the instruments from sun and rain but e still allow air waka reach the instruments well well. Na why option D correct.

questions.q: The temperature in Jos was recorded four times in one day as follows: 6am = 18°C, 12noon = 27°C, 6pm = 23°C, 12midnight = 16°C. Calculate the mean daily temperature for that day.
questions.e: Mean temperature is found by adding all the readings and dividing by the number of readings. 18+27+23+16 = 84, and 84 divided by 4 gives 21°C.
questions.p: To find mean temperature, you go add all the readings together then divide by how many readings dem be. 18+27+23+16 = 84, 84 divided by 4 na 21°C.

questions.q: On a cool harmattan morning in Kano, moisture in the air condenses into tiny water droplets that settle on blades of grass as dew. This condensation happens when the air cools down to a particular temperature known as the:
questions.e: The dew point is the temperature at which air becomes saturated with water vapour, causing the excess moisture to condense into liquid droplets such as dew. It is different from the boiling, melting or freezing points, which relate to changes of state in water itself, not to air saturation.
questions.p: Dew point na the temperature wey air go reach before e saturate well-well, make the water vapour turn to small-small water (dew). E no be the same thing as boiling, melting or freezing point wey dey about water change form.

questions.q: Which of the following is the major natural vegetation type found in the equatorial rainforest belt of southern Nigeria, where trees usually form three distinct canopy layers (storeys)?
questions.e: The equatorial rainforest has tall evergreen trees arranged in layers (upper, middle and lower storeys) due to high rainfall and temperature all year round. Guinea, Sudan and Sahel vegetation are savanna types found further north with less rainfall.
questions.p: Equatorial rainforest get big tall trees wey dey arrange for layers (storeys) because rain plus heat plenty throughout the year. Guinea, Sudan and Sahel na savanna wey dey north where rain no too plenty.

questions.q: A region in West Africa has annual rainfall of about 1500mm to 2000mm, well distributed throughout the year with no marked dry season, and mean monthly temperature of about 26°C all year round. Which climate type does this describe?
questions.e: High, well-distributed rainfall with no clear dry season and constant warm temperature is typical of the equatorial climate, found in places like the Niger Delta. The other climates all have a marked dry season.
questions.p: Plenty rain wey dey fall well-well throughout the year with no serious dry season, plus steady hot weather, na equatorial climate like we see for Niger Delta. The other climates get clear dry season.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the rainfall pattern of the Sahel (Sudan-Sahel) climate region of West Africa?
o: Rainfall throughout the year with no dry season
Rainfall occurs mainly in winter with dry summers
A short rainy season of about 3 to 4 months followed by a long dry season
Two distinct wet seasons separated by two dry seasons
questions.e: The Sahel lies far from the sea and the ITD only reaches it briefly, giving a short wet season of 3-4 months and a long dry season for the rest of the year. The other options describe equatorial or Mediterranean patterns, not the Sahel.
questions.p: Sahel dey far from sea, so rain only dey fall small time (3-4 months) then long dry season follow. The other options na equatorial or Mediterranean pattern, no be Sahel own.

questions.q: As one travels from the coast of Nigeria northward towards the Sahara Desert, which of the following correctly shows the order of natural vegetation belts encountered?
o: Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna, Rainforest
Guinea savanna, Rainforest, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
Sudan savanna, Rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sahel savanna
Rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
questions.e: Rainfall decreases as one moves from the coast northward, so vegetation changes from rainforest near the coast, through Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, to Sahel savanna near the Sahara. This order matches the decreasing rainfall pattern of Nigeria.
questions.p: Rain dey reduce as you dey move from coast go north, so vegetation go change from rainforest near coast, pass Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, reach Sahel savanna near Sahara. Na the rain pattern cause am.

questions.q: The equatorial climate region typically experiences two rainfall maxima (peaks) in a year. What is the main reason for this pattern?
o: The region receives moist winds from two different oceans at the same time
The overhead sun (and the Inter-Tropical Discontinuity) passes over the region twice a year, around April and October
Ocean currents along the coast change direction twice a year
The region is surrounded by mountains that cause orographic rainfall twice a year
questions.e: The sun appears to move between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, crossing the equator around the equinoxes (March/April and September/October). Each time it is overhead, it drags the ITD and heavy convectional rain with it, giving two rainfall peaks. The other options are not the actual cause of this pattern.
questions.p: Sun dey waka between Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn, e dey cross equator for March/April and September/October. Any time e dey overhead, e dey carry ITD and heavy rain come, so na why peak rain dey show twice. The other options no be the real reason.

questions.q: Kano lies in the Sudan savanna interior of Nigeria while Lagos lies in the equatorial coastal belt. Which statement correctly compares their annual temperature ranges and gives the right reason?
o: Kano has a higher annual temperature range than Lagos because it is far from the moderating influence of the sea
Lagos has a higher annual temperature range than Kano because it is nearer to the equator
Both cities have the same annual temperature range because they are in the same country
Kano has a lower annual temperature range than Lagos because it lies near the desert margin
questions.e: Lagos, being coastal, has its temperature moderated by sea breezes, giving a small annual range. Kano, deep inland, lacks this moderating effect, so it experiences much hotter days and cooler nights/harmattan periods, giving a wider annual temperature range.
questions.p: Lagos dey near sea, so sea breeze dey cool the weather, e no get wide range of temperature. Kano dey far inside land, no sea to cool am, so e get hot day and cold harmattan night, wey make the range wide pass Lagos own.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the Mediterranean type of climate found along parts of the North African coast (such as northern Morocco and Tunisia)?
o: Warm dry summers and mild wet winters
Cold dry summers and hot wet winters
Hot wet summers and cool dry winters
Uniformly hot and wet throughout the year
questions.e: The Mediterranean climate is known for warm, dry summers caused by subtropical high pressure, and mild, wet winters when the westerlies and low pressure systems bring rain. This is the opposite of the equatorial pattern of year-round heat and rain.
questions.p: Mediterranean climate get warm dry summer (because of high pressure) and mild wet winter (because of westerlies and rain). E different from equatorial wey hot and wet dey throughout the year.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT usually listed among the major factors responsible for the formation of soil?
questions.e: Soil formation (pedogenesis) is controlled by climate, parent rock, relief, living organisms and time. Population density affects how soil is used, not how it is formed, so it is not a factor of soil formation.
questions.p: How soil dey form na climate, parent rock, relief, living things and time dey cause am. Population density na about how many people dey use the land, e no dey form soil.

questions.q: A geography teacher tells her class that soil texture refers specifically to a certain property of soil. Which statement correctly defines soil texture?
o: The colour of the soil as seen with the naked eye
The way soil particles are arranged into crumbs or clods
The level of acidity or alkalinity of the soil
The relative proportion of sand, silt and clay particles in a soil sample
questions.e: Soil texture is determined by the proportions of sand, silt and clay particles in the soil, which decides whether it is sandy, loamy or clayey. The arrangement into crumbs is called soil structure, not texture.
questions.p: Soil texture na how sand, silt and clay particles mix inside the soil, e be the one wey tell us if soil na sandy, loamy or clay. The way the particles dey arrange into crumbs na soil structure, no be texture.

questions.q: Laterite soils, which are common in many parts of tropical West Africa including Nigeria, mainly develop as a result of which process?
o: Wind-blown deposition of fine desert particles
Accumulation of frozen organic matter in cold regions
Heavy leaching of silica under intense rainfall, leaving behind iron and aluminium oxides
Chemical weathering of limestone rocks alone
questions.e: In areas with heavy rainfall and high temperatures, silica is washed (leached) out of the soil, leaving behind iron and aluminium oxides that give laterite its reddish colour and hard crust. This process is typical of tropical regions like West Africa.
questions.p: Where rain dey plenty and e hot well well, water go wash away silica from soil, leave iron and aluminium oxide wey make laterite red and hard. Na this kind thing dey happen for tropical place like West Africa.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State has a sloping farmland that suffers heavy soil erosion during the rainy season. Which farming practice would best reduce the erosion by slowing down the speed of running water down the slope?
o: Contour ploughing (ploughing along the slope's contour lines)
questions.e: Contour ploughing involves making ridges or furrows that run across the slope rather than up and down it. This traps water and slows its flow, reducing soil erosion on sloping land.
questions.p: Contour ploughing na when farmer make ridge across the slope instead of up and down. E dey hold water make e no run fast, so e dey reduce how soil dey wash away for slope land.

questions.q: A moist soil sample taken from a farm in Oyo State has a total volume of 500 cm^3. Laboratory analysis shows that air spaces occupy 150 cm^3 and water occupies 100 cm^3, while the rest of the volume is made up of solid soil particles. What percentage of the sample is made up of solid particles?
questions.e: Solid particles = total volume minus (air + water) = 500 - (150 + 100) = 250 cm^3. Percentage of solids = (250/500) x 100 = 50%.
questions.p: Solid particles na total volume minus (air add water) = 500 - (150 + 100) = 250 cm^3. Percentage of solid = (250/500) x 100 = 50%.

questions.q: A farmer near Kano tests his soil and finds that the pH is 4.5, which is too acidic for his maize crop that grows best at pH 6 to 7. Which treatment would most likely help to correct this soil for better maize growth?
o: Adding common table salt to the soil
Adding more decomposed organic acid to the soil
Adding lime (calcium carbonate) to the soil
questions.e: Lime (calcium carbonate) reacts with excess hydrogen ions in acidic soil, raising the pH towards neutral. This makes the soil less acidic and more suitable for crops like maize that prefer a pH close to neutral.
questions.p: Lime (calcium carbonate) dey react with the excess hydrogen wey dey make soil acidic, e go raise the pH go near neutral. This one go make the soil better for maize wey like pH wey near neutral.

questions.q: Which of the following natural resources is classified as renewable?
questions.e: Renewable resources can be replaced naturally within a short time or are not used up, like sunlight, wind and water. Crude oil, natural gas and coal are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form, so they are non-renewable.
questions.p: Renewable resource na di one wey fit replace quick or no dey finish, like sunlight, wind and water. Crude oil, gas and coal na fossil fuel wey take plenty millions of years to form, so dem no dey renewable.

questions.q: In the Sahel region of West Africa, which human activity contributes most to the spread of desertification?
questions.e: Overgrazing removes the grass cover that protects the soil, leaving it bare and exposed to wind erosion, which speeds up desert encroachment. Afforestation, terracing and crop rotation are conservation practices that actually reduce desertification.
questions.p: Overgrazing dey remove di grass wey dey cover and protect di soil, so di soil go bare and wind go easily blow am comot, dis one dey speed up desert spreading. Afforestation, terracing and crop rotation na good conservation methods wey dey reduce desertification.

questions.q: Which farming method is most effective for controlling soil erosion on a steep hillside farm in a hilly part of Nigeria such as the Jos Plateau?
o: Planting crops in straight rows running up and down the slope
questions.e: Terracing breaks a steep slope into flat steps, which slows down the speed of surface run-off and reduces soil erosion. Planting up-and-down the slope, clearing vegetation and bush burning all leave the soil loose and expose it to faster run-off and erosion.
questions.p: Terracing dey turn steep slope to flat steps, e dey slow down how water dey run so e no go wash away di soil quick. If you plant up-and-down di slope, clear di bush or burn am, di soil go loose and run-off go wash am away fast.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a man-made (human-induced) environmental hazard?
o: Oil spillage from a damaged pipeline
questions.e: Oil spillage happens because of human activities such as poor pipeline maintenance or vandalism, so it is man-made. Earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and tsunamis are natural hazards caused by processes inside the earth, not by human action.
questions.p: Oil spillage dey happen because of human activity like bad pipeline maintenance or vandalism, so na man-made hazard. Earthquake, volcanic eruption and tsunami na natural hazard wey dey come from inside di earth, no be human cause am.

questions.q: One major long-term effect of large-scale deforestation on the climate of an area is that it leads to
o: an improvement in underground water quality
questions.e: Trees release moisture into the air through transpiration, which helps in cloud formation and rainfall. When forests are cleared on a large scale, less moisture enters the atmosphere, so the area tends to receive less rainfall over time.
questions.p: Trees dey release water vapour go air through transpiration, and dis one dey help cloud form and bring rain. If dem clear plenty forest, less water vapour go dey enter air, so di place rainfall go reduce small small.

questions.q: A farming community in a dry part of northern Nigeria has noticed over 20 years that crop yields are falling, the water table is dropping, and sand dunes are creeping closer to their farmland. Which conservation measure would best address this problem?
o: Allowing more cattle to graze freely on the remaining grassland
Clearing more bush to expand land for mechanised farming
Draining nearby wetlands to create more irrigation channels
Constructing shelterbelts and planting drought-resistant trees around the farmland
questions.e: Shelterbelts (rows of trees) break the force of the wind, reduce soil moisture loss, and stop sand dunes from advancing onto farmland, while drought-resistant trees help restore vegetation cover. The other options would worsen the problem by removing more vegetation or increasing pressure on the land and water.
questions.p: Shelterbelt (tree rows) dey break wind force, reduce how moisture dey comot from soil, and e dey stop sand dunes from reaching di farmland, and drought-resistant trees go help bring back vegetation. Di other options go make di matter worse because dem go remove more plants or put more pressure for land and water.

questions.q: Severe gully erosion is a common environmental hazard in parts of southeastern Nigeria (such as Anambra and Imo States) but less common in the drier parts of northern Nigeria. Which reason best explains this difference?
o: The north receives higher annual rainfall than the south
The north has steeper slopes than the south
The south has loose, sandy soils combined with high rainfall intensity
The south has more rocky terrain that resists erosion
questions.e: Southeastern Nigeria has loose, poorly compacted sandy/lateritic soils, and it also receives heavy, intense rainfall; the combination of weak soil structure and strong run-off cuts deep gullies. The north, by contrast, has lower rainfall and often more compact or rocky soils, so gully erosion is less severe there.
questions.p: Southeast Nigeria get loose sandy or lateritic soil wey no tight well, plus heavy strong rain, so di soil dey easily wash comot make deep gully. North get less rain and di soil dey more hard or rocky, so gully erosion no too plenty for dia side.

questions.q: On a map with a scale of 1 : 50 000, what does the scale indicate?
o: The ground distance is always 50 000 times smaller than the map distance
One unit of measurement on the map represents 50 000 of the same unit on the ground
The map is exactly 50 000 times smaller than the actual area in square kilometres
One centimetre on the map equals 50 000 kilometres on the ground
questions.e: A representative fraction such as 1:50 000 means one unit on the map stands for 50 000 of the same unit on the ground (e.g. 1 cm = 50 000 cm). It is a linear ratio, not an area ratio, and the units must be the same before conversion.
questions.p: Wen dem write scale as 1:50 000, e mean say one unit for map na 50 000 of di same unit for ground, like 1cm = 50 000cm. Na straight distance ratio, e no be area ratio, and di units must match before you convert am.

questions.q: On a topographical map drawn to a scale of 1 : 25 000, the straight-line distance between Ijebu-Ode market and Oru junction measured 8.4 cm. What is the actual ground distance between the two places, in kilometres?
questions.e: Ground distance = 8.4 cm x 25 000 = 210 000 cm. Since 1 km = 100 000 cm, 210 000 cm divided by 100 000 gives 2.1 km. So the two places are 2.1 km apart on the ground.
questions.p: Ground distance = 8.4cm x 25 000 = 210 000cm. Since 1km na 100 000cm, 210 000cm divide by 100 000 e give 2.1km. So di two places dey 2.1km apart for ground.

questions.q: A surveyor standing at point X observes that point Y is directly to the north-east of him. What is the bearing of Y from X?
questions.e: Bearings are measured clockwise from north. North-east lies exactly halfway between north (000°) and east (090°), which is 045°. The other options represent east, south-east and north-west respectively.
questions.p: Dem dey measure bearing clockwise from north. North-east dey exactly between north (000°) and east (090°), so e be 045°. Di oda options na east, south-east and north-west.

questions.q: A hiker walks from Village A to Village B on a bearing of 062°. What is the bearing of Village A from Village B (the back bearing)?
questions.e: To get the back bearing, add 180° when the original bearing is less than 180°. So 062° + 180° = 242°. This gives the direction of A as seen from B.
questions.p: To find back bearing, if di first bearing dey less than 180°, you go add 180°. So 062° + 180° = 242°. Na dis one be di direction of A if you dey look am from B.

questions.q: A map is drawn to a scale of 1 : 50 000. The area of a forest reserve measured on the map is 6 square centimetres. What is the actual area of the forest reserve on the ground, in square kilometres?
questions.e: For area, the scale factor must be squared: 50 000^2 = 2 500 000 000. Ground area = 6 cm^2 x 2 500 000 000 = 15 000 000 000 cm^2. Since 1 km^2 = 100 000^2 cm^2 = 10 000 000 000 cm^2, dividing gives 15 000 000 000 / 10 000 000 000 = 1.5 km^2.
questions.p: For area, you must square di scale: 50 000^2 = 2 500 000 000. Ground area = 6cm^2 x 2 500 000 000 = 15 000 000 000cm^2. Since 1km^2 na 10 000 000 000cm^2, if you divide e give 1.5km^2.

questions.q: A written description of a map area says: 'The land rises gradually from 50 metres above sea level at the coastline to 450 metres at the northern boundary, and the contour lines are spaced far apart throughout the area.' What type of relief does this description suggest?
o: A deep valley with sharp cliffs on both sides
A steep escarpment rising abruptly from the coast
A flat lowland with no change in elevation
A gently sloping plain rising steadily inland
questions.e: Widely spaced contour lines show a gentle, gradual slope rather than a steep one. Since the height increases slowly and evenly from 50 m to 450 m, the land is a gently sloping plain, not a cliff, valley or flat lowland.
questions.p: Wen contour lines dey far from each oda, e mean say di slope dey gentle, e no steep. Since di height dey rise small small from 50m to 450m, na gentle plain, e no be cliff, valley or flat land.

questions.q: A statistical chart that uses small pictures or symbols, each representing a fixed quantity, to display data is called a:
questions.e: A pictogram uses repeated small pictures or symbols, where each symbol stands for a fixed number of items, to show statistical data in a simple visual way.
questions.p: Pictogram na chart wey dey use small pictures or symbols, where each one dey represent fixed number, to show data for simple way.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State cultivates four crops on his 80-hectare farm as follows: Yam 20 hectares, Cassava 24 hectares, Maize 16 hectares and Rice 20 hectares. If this information is drawn as a pie chart, what angle would represent the area under Cassava?
questions.e: To find the angle for Cassava, divide its area by the total area and multiply by 360 degrees: (24/80) x 360 = 108°.
questions.p: To find the angle for Cassava, divide the area wey e cover by total area, multiply by 360: (24/80) x 360 = 108°.

questions.q: A bar chart shows the monthly rainfall of a town for five months as follows: January 50mm, February 70mm, March 120mm, April 160mm and May 200mm. What is the average monthly rainfall for the five months?
questions.e: Add all the values: 50+70+120+160+200 = 600mm, then divide by the number of months (5): 600/5 = 120mm.
questions.p: Add all the numbers: 50+70+120+160+200 = 600mm, then divide am by 5 months: 600/5 = 120mm.

questions.q: A pie chart shows how a family's monthly income of ₦60,000 is shared: Food takes an angle of 150°, Rent takes 90°, Transport takes 60°, and the rest goes to Savings. How much money is spent on Savings?
questions.e: The angle for Savings is 360 - (150+90+60) = 60°. Since 360° represents ₦60,000, the Savings amount is (60/360) x 60,000 = ₦10,000.
questions.p: The angle for Savings na 360 - (150+90+60) = 60°. Since 360° na ₦60,000, Savings go be (60/360) x 60,000 = ₦10,000.

questions.q: A map that uses different shades or colours to show the varying intensity of a statistical variable, such as population density, within fixed boundaries like states or local government areas, is known as a:
questions.e: A choropleth map uses shading or colour variation within defined boundaries to represent differences in a statistical value, such as density or output.
questions.p: Choropleth map na map wey dey use different shade or colour inside clear boundary (like state) to show difference for statistical value like density.

questions.q: A line graph shows the population of a village as follows: 1990 - 4,000 people, 2000 - 6,000 people, 2010 - 10,000 people. What was the average annual increase in population between 2000 and 2010?
questions.e: The increase between 2000 and 2010 is 10,000 - 6,000 = 4,000 over 10 years, so the average yearly increase is 4,000/10 = 400.
questions.p: The increase from 2000 to 2010 na 10,000 - 6,000 = 4,000 for 10 years, so average yearly increase na 4,000/10 = 400.

questions.q: On a dot map of a region, each dot stands for 2,000 people. If a particular local government area on the map is represented by 15 dots, what is the estimated population of that area?
questions.e: Since each dot represents 2,000 people, the total population is found by multiplying the number of dots by the value per dot: 15 x 2,000 = 30,000.
questions.p: Since each dot mean 2,000 people, multiply number of dots by the value for each dot: 15 x 2,000 = 30,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines population density?
o: The total number of people living in a country
The ratio of males to females in a population
The number of people per unit area of land
The rate at which population increases over time
questions.e: Population density measures how many people live within a given area of land, usually expressed as persons per square kilometre. It shows how crowded or sparse a place is, not the total number of people or growth rate.
questions.p: Population density na how many people dey live for one area of land, like per square kilometre. E no be di total number of people or how fast population dey grow.

questions.q: Which of the following factors is most likely to attract a dense population settlement in a West African country?
o: Fertile alluvial plains suitable for farming
Dense tropical rainforest with poor drainage
questions.e: Fertile alluvial plains support good crop yields and easy farming, which attracts many settlers and leads to dense population. Mountains, swampy forests and dry arid lands discourage large settlements because they make farming and movement difficult.
questions.p: Fertile land wey good for farming dey attract plenty people because dem fit get good harvest. Mountain, swampy forest and dry desert no good for farming so people no dey settle well there.

questions.q: A town in Enugu State has a population of 450,000 people and covers a land area of 1,500 square kilometres. Calculate the population density of the town.
questions.e: Population density = population / area = 450,000 / 1,500 = 300 persons per km^2. The other options come from simple division errors.
questions.p: Density = population divide by area, na 450,000 divide by 1,500 wey be 300 persons per km^2. Di other answers na from wrong division.

questions.q: A population pyramid for a developing West African country typically shows a wide base that narrows rapidly towards the apex. Which population characteristic does this shape best represent?
o: Low birth rate and high life expectancy
Equal number of males and females at all ages
High rate of out-migration of young adults
High birth rate with a large proportion of young people
questions.e: A wide base in a population pyramid means many babies and young children are being born, showing a high birth rate. The rapid narrowing towards the top shows fewer people surviving to old age, typical of developing countries like those in West Africa.
questions.p: Wide base for population pyramid mean say plenty pikin dey born, na high birth rate be dat. Di quick narrow for top mean say few people dey reach old age, wey be common ting for developing kontri.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major cause of rural-urban migration in Nigeria?
o: Abundant fertile farmland in rural areas
Government policy restricting movement into cities
Search for better job opportunities and social amenities in cities
Lower cost of living in urban centres compared to rural areas
questions.e: People move from villages to cities mainly because cities offer more jobs, schools, hospitals and other amenities. Rural areas usually lack these facilities, pushing young people to migrate to urban centres.
questions.p: People dey japa from village go city mostly because city get work, school, hospital and other better things. Village no too get dis facilities, so young ones dey move go city.

questions.q: In a certain Local Government Area, the birth rate is 42 per 1000 people and the death rate is 14 per 1000 people per year. Calculate the rate of natural increase of the population, expressed as a percentage.
questions.e: Natural increase rate = (Birth rate - Death rate)/1000 x 100 = (42-14)/1000 x 100 = 28/1000 x 100 = 2.8%. The other options result from forgetting to divide by 1000 or doubling the value.
questions.p: Natural increase = (birth rate minus death rate) divide by 1000, multiply by 100, na (42-14)/1000 x 100 = 2.8%. Di other answers na from forgetting to divide by 1000 or doubling am.

questions.q: A community has 2,500 children aged 0-14 years, 2,000 elderly persons aged 65 years and above, and 9,000 people within the working age group of 15-64 years. Calculate the dependency ratio of the community, expressed as a percentage.
questions.e: Dependency ratio = (dependents / working population) x 100 = (2,500 + 2,000) / 9,000 x 100 = 4,500/9,000 x 100 = 50%. This shows that for every 100 working people, 50 dependents (young and old) depend on them.
questions.p: Dependency ratio = (dependants divide by working population) x 100, na (2,500+2,000)/9,000 x 100 = 50%. Dis mean say for every 100 working people, 50 dependants (young and old) dey depend on dem.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a nucleated settlement?
o: Houses built only inside river valleys
Houses built in a straight line along a road
Houses scattered far apart from one another across farmland
Houses closely clustered together around a central point such as a market, water source or place of worship
questions.e: A nucleated settlement is one where houses and buildings are grouped closely together around a central feature like a market, well or shrine. This clustering happens because people want to be near a shared resource or facility.
questions.p: Nucleated settlement na where houses pack together near one common place like market, well or shrine. Na because people wan dey close to that important place make dem build like that.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major factor that influences where the site of a new settlement is first chosen?
questions.e: Early settlers always looked for places with a reliable source of water for drinking, cooking, washing and farming before building a settlement. Without water, a settlement cannot survive, so it is a key site factor.
questions.p: People wey dey find where to settle go first check if water dey near, because dem need am for drink, cook and farm. Without water, settlement no fit survive, so e dey important well well.

questions.q: Onitsha grew into an important settlement partly because it developed at the point along the River Niger where traders and travellers cross by bridge, and where goods brought from different directions are exchanged before being sent out to other towns. Based on this description, which major function does Onitsha perform?
questions.e: A settlement located at a crossing point on a river, where goods are gathered and then sent out to other places, is performing a collecting-and-distributing or route-centre function. This is common for towns built at bridging points like Onitsha on the River Niger.
questions.p: When town dey grow for river crossing point, where traders dey bring goods come exchange am before dem send am go other towns, na collecting and distributing (route centre) function the town dey perform. Na so Onitsha take dey important for trade for Niger area.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a settlement pattern with its correct description?
o: Radial pattern - isolated homesteads scattered with no particular arrangement
Dispersed pattern - houses scattered far apart, often one family to a farm
Linear pattern - houses built in a circular arrangement around a point
Nucleated pattern - houses built in a single line along a valley
questions.e: A dispersed settlement pattern is one where individual houses or homesteads are widely scattered, usually because each family lives on its own farmland rather than close to neighbours. The other options wrongly swap the descriptions with the wrong pattern names.
questions.p: Dispersed pattern na when houses scatter far from each other, mostly because each family dey live for dia own farmland. The other options mix up the correct description with the wrong pattern name.

questions.q: A certain settlement was built on top of a hill, with swampy land surrounding it on all sides. What is the most likely reason the early settlers chose this site?
o: Defence against attack and protection from seasonal flooding
Easy access to markets in nearby towns
questions.e: Hilltops surrounded by swamps are naturally difficult for enemies or wild animals to approach, and they stay dry during floods. Early communities often chose such sites mainly for safety and protection rather than for farming or trade convenience.
questions.p: Hill wey swamp surround dey hard for enemy or wild animal to enter, and e no dey flood easily. Old communities dey choose dat kind place mainly for safety, no be for farming or market reasons.

questions.q: In a region, a village has only one primary school and a weekly market; a town in the same region has a secondary school, a general hospital and a daily market; while the regional city has a university, specialist hospitals and several large markets. Which factor best explains why the city offers far more functions and services than the village?
o: The city is located farther away from all major roads
The city has fewer administrative buildings than the village
The city has a larger population and a wider sphere of influence, requiring more services
The city has a smaller population to serve than the village
questions.e: In a settlement hierarchy, higher-order settlements like cities serve a much larger population and a wider surrounding area, so they need and can support more specialised services such as universities and specialist hospitals. Villages, with small populations and limited reach, only need basic low-order services.
questions.p: For settlement hierarchy, big settlement like city dey serve plenty people and wide area, so e need plenty special services like university and specialist hospital. Village small small, dem just need basic things like primary school and small market.

questions.q: In a cocoa-farming community, a geography class observed that houses are built very far apart from one another, with each family living directly on its own large cocoa farmland instead of gathering in a central village. Which settlement pattern best describes this arrangement, and why?
o: Nucleated settlement, because of communal land ownership
Radial settlement, because houses surround a central market
Dispersed settlement, because of the nature of extensive farming
Linear settlement, because houses follow the road network
questions.e: When farming requires large pieces of land, families tend to live right on their farms rather than travelling daily from a central village, which spreads the houses far apart. This widely scattered arrangement, caused by the need for extensive land, is called a dispersed settlement pattern.
questions.p: Where farming need plenty land, families go just dey live for dia own farm instead of waka come and go from one central village. That kind wide scattered arrangement, wey land need cause am, na dispersed settlement pattern.

questions.q: Which mode of transport is most suitable for conveying crude oil over long distances, such as from oil fields in the Niger Delta to refineries or export terminals?
questions.e: Pipelines are specially built to carry liquids and gases like crude oil continuously over long distances at low cost. Road, rail and air transport are not designed for bulk liquid cargo of this nature.
questions.p: Pipeline na the correct answer because dem build am well well to dey carry liquid like crude oil for long distance cheap cheap. Road, rail and air no fit carry am well like that.

questions.q: The exchange of goods and services between two or more different countries is best described as what type of trade?
questions.e: International trade is trade that takes place across national boundaries, between one country and another. Internal and retail trade happen within a country, while barter trade simply means exchanging goods without money.
questions.p: International trade na when goods and services dey exchange between different countries. Internal and retail trade dey happen inside one country, while barter trade just mean exchange goods without money.

questions.q: What is the major advantage of water transport over road transport when moving bulky goods like timber and cement over long distances?
o: It gives greater flexibility of routes
It is faster than road transport
It is less affected by weather conditions
It has lower cost per tonne for bulky goods
questions.e: Water transport can carry very large loads at once, which greatly reduces the cost per tonne compared to road transport. It is actually slower, less flexible in route choice, and more affected by weather such as storms.
questions.p: Water transport fit carry plenty load for once, so e dey cheap pass road transport for each tonne. But e slow pass road, e no too flexible, and weather like storm fit affect am well well.

questions.q: A railway line is to be built through a rugged highland area with steep slopes, such as parts of the Jos Plateau. Which physical factor would most limit the construction of this railway?
o: Low population density in the area
High cost of tunneling and constructing gentle gradients
Absence of mineral resources along the route
questions.e: Railways need fairly gentle, even gradients to allow trains to move safely and efficiently. In rugged highlands, engineers must cut tunnels, build bridges and level slopes, which greatly raises construction cost and difficulty, more than population or rainfall issues.
questions.p: Train need gentle road wey no too steep to waka well. For rugged highland, dem go need tunnel, bridge and level di ground, wey go cost plenty money and wahala pass population or rain matter.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) with regard to trade among member countries?
o: To promote free movement of goods and persons among member states
To build railway lines linking Europe and West Africa
To control global crude oil prices
To regulate international air traffic rules
questions.e: ECOWAS was formed mainly to encourage economic cooperation and integration, including free movement of goods, services and persons among West African member states. It does not control global oil prices or manage worldwide air traffic.
questions.p: ECOWAS main work na to encourage economic cooperation and free movement of goods, services and people among West African member countries. Dem no dey control world oil price or world air traffic.

questions.q: Which farming system involves clearing a piece of forest land, cultivating it for two or three years, and then abandoning it for several years to allow the natural vegetation and soil fertility to return?
questions.e: Shifting cultivation is the practice of farming a plot for a short period and then moving to a new plot, leaving the old one to fallow and regain fertility naturally. This is common in traditional farming communities in West Africa.
questions.p: Shifting cultivation na when farmer clear bush, farm am small time, den comot go another place make the land rest and regain strength. Na common practice for village farming for West Africa.

questions.q: A farming practice in which a farmer rears animals such as goats and poultry alongside growing crops like maize and cassava on the same farmland is best described as:
questions.e: Mixed farming is the combination of crop cultivation and animal rearing on the same farm. This allows the farmer to use animal waste as manure and crop residue as animal feed.
questions.p: Mixed farming na when farmer dey grow crops and dey rear animals for the same farm. E good because animal dung fit be manure, and crop waste fit feed the animals.

questions.q: The main reason farmers practice crop rotation, where different crops are grown in a fixed sequence on the same piece of land over successive seasons, is to:
o: Increase the size of farmland available
Encourage permanent cropping of a single crop
Reduce the need for farm labourers
Maintain soil fertility and reduce pest and disease build-up
questions.e: Different crops take up and return different nutrients to the soil, so rotating them prevents the soil from losing specific nutrients. It also breaks the life cycle of pests and diseases that attack a particular crop.
questions.p: Different crops dey use and return different nutrients for soil, so if you rotate them, soil no go lose one type of nutrient finish. E also dey break the cycle of pest and disease wey dey attack one particular crop.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine disadvantage of mechanized farming for an average Nigerian smallholder farmer?
o: It completely removes the need for fertile soil
It increases soil erosion when used on steep or poorly managed land
It makes land preparation slower than manual methods
It always leads to lower crop yield per hectare
questions.e: Heavy machinery like tractors and ploughs can break up soil structure and expose bare soil to wind and rain, especially on slopes, leading to erosion. Mechanization actually speeds up land preparation and can raise yields, so the other options are wrong.
questions.p: Heavy machine like tractor fit break the soil structure and expose am to wind and rain, especially for sloppy land, and e go cause erosion. Mechanization dey make work faster and fit increase yield, so the other options no correct.

questions.q: A cooperative farm in Oyo State has a total area of 12 hectares. The farm is divided into 4 equal plots for a 4-year crop rotation cycle: yam, maize, groundnut, and fallow, one crop (or fallow) per plot each year. What is the size, in hectares, of the plot left fallow in any given year?
questions.e: The 12 hectares is divided equally among 4 plots, so each plot is 12/4 = 3 hectares. Since one plot is fallow each year, the fallow plot is 3 hectares.
questions.p: Dem divide the 12 hectares into 4 equal plots, so 12/4 = 3 hectares be each plot size. Since one plot dey fallow every year, na 3 hectares be the fallow land.

questions.q: Cocoa is widely cultivated in the forest belt of southern Nigeria (such as Ondo and Osun States) but is not grown commercially in the far northern parts of the country. The main reason for this difference is:
o: Cocoa trees cannot survive in soils with laterite content
Northern soils lack any mineral nutrients
Cocoa requires heavy, well-distributed rainfall and high humidity, which the north lacks
Northern farmers are not interested in tree crops
questions.e: Cocoa is a tropical tree crop that needs high rainfall (over 1,500 mm annually, well distributed) and high humidity, conditions found in the forest belt of the south. The drier savanna climate of the north does not support cocoa growth.
questions.p: Cocoa na tropical tree crop wey need plenty rain (pass 1500mm every year) and high humidity, and na so the forest area for south be. The dry savanna climate for north no fit support cocoa.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue State harvested 3,600 kg of maize from a 6-hectare farm before using fertilizer. After applying fertilizer the following season on the same farm size, he harvested 4,800 kg. By how many kilograms per hectare did his yield increase?
questions.e: Before fertilizer: 3600/6 = 600 kg per hectare. After fertilizer: 4800/6 = 800 kg per hectare. The increase is 800 - 600 = 200 kg per hectare.
questions.p: Before fertilizer: 3600/6 = 600 kg per hectare. After fertilizer: 4800/6 = 800 kg per hectare. The increase na 800 - 600 = 200 kg per hectare.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines a manufacturing industry?
o: The extraction of raw materials from the earth
The transportation of goods from factory to market
The processing of raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods
The buying and selling of finished goods to consumers
questions.e: Manufacturing is the stage where raw materials are changed into useful finished or semi-finished products. Extraction, transportation and selling are separate economic activities that come before or after manufacturing.
questions.p: Manufacturing na when dem dey process raw materials turn am to finished or semi-finished product. To dig raw material, carry goods go market, or sell am na different work from manufacturing.

questions.q: A company wants to build a cement factory. Which factor should mainly guide the choice of location?
o: Nearness to the coast for fishing
questions.e: Cement is made mainly from limestone, so cement factories are raw-material oriented and are usually sited close to limestone deposits to reduce the cost of transporting heavy, bulky materials. Fishing, fashion design and universities have no direct link to cement production.
questions.p: Cement dem dey make am from limestone, so cement factory dey site near where limestone dey so dem no go spend plenty money carry the heavy material comot far. Fishing coast, fashion designer or university no get anything do with cement production.

questions.q: A footloose industry is one whose location is not tied to any particular raw material source and can be sited almost anywhere with good transport and market access. Which of the following best illustrates a footloose industry?
o: Sugar refinery sited near sugarcane plantation
Electronics assembly plant that can locate anywhere with good transport links
Iron and steel industry near iron ore deposits
questions.e: Electronics assembly uses light, already-processed components, so it is not tied to a bulky raw material source and can be located wherever transport and market conditions are favourable. The other three industries must stay close to their bulky raw materials, so they are not footloose.
questions.p: Electronics assembly dey use light component wey don already process, so e no need to dey near any heavy raw material, e fit site anywhere wey transport and market good. The other three must stay close to their raw material, so na footloose industry be the electronics one.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major problem facing manufacturing industries in Nigeria?
o: Frequent power outages and poor infrastructural facilities
questions.e: Many Nigerian manufacturing firms suffer from frequent power cuts and poor roads, railways and water supply, which raise production costs and reduce output. The other options describe favourable conditions that are generally not the real situation facing most industries.
questions.p: Plenty factory for Nigeria dey suffer from NEPA/PHCN wahala and bad road, water and other infrastructure, dis one dey increase cost and reduce production. The other options na good condition wey no dey match wetin dey happen for ground.

questions.q: In the industrial area of Aba, Nigeria, many small factories making shoes, bags and clothing are deliberately located close to one another so that they can share common facilities such as electricity, water supply and road access, thereby reducing production costs for all of them. This situation best illustrates which concept?
questions.e: Agglomeration economies occur when firms locate close together to share infrastructure and services, lowering costs for everyone involved, exactly as described for Aba. Industrial inertia refers to staying at an old site even after the original advantage disappears, vertical integration refers to combining production stages of the same firm, and import substitution means producing locally what was formerly imported.
questions.p: Agglomeration economies na when factories dey site near each other so dem fit share light, water and road, dis one dey reduce cost for everybody, na so e dey happen for Aba. Industrial inertia na when factory remain for old location even though the first advantage don gone, vertical integration na when one company combine different stages of production, import substitution na when dem begin produce wetin dem used to import.

questions.q: A textile mill in Kaduna produces 3600 metres of cloth every 6 hours of steady operation. If the mill keeps working at this same constant rate for 10 hours in a day, how many metres of cloth will it produce that day?
questions.e: First find the rate per hour: 3600 metres divided by 6 hours equals 600 metres per hour. Multiplying this rate by 10 hours gives 600 x 10 = 6000 metres for the day.
questions.p: First find how much cloth dem dey produce for one hour: 3600 divide by 6 na 600 metres per hour. Multiply the 600 by 10 hours, e go be 6000 metres for the whole day.

questions.q: The Sokoto-Rima river basin, known for its wheat and rice irrigation schemes, is located in which geographical region of Nigeria?
questions.e: The Sokoto-Rima basin lies in Sokoto and Kebbi States, which are in the North-West geopolitical region of Nigeria. This area is known for irrigation farming such as the Bakolori project.
questions.p: Sokoto-Rima river basin dey for Sokoto and Kebbi States, wey be North-West region of Nigeria. Na there dem dey do irrigation farming like Bakolori project.

questions.q: Which type of natural vegetation is most characteristic of the Niger Delta region of Nigeria?
questions.e: The Niger Delta is a low-lying, waterlogged coastal area with many creeks and estuaries, which supports mangrove swamp forest. This vegetation has stilt roots that survive in salty, tidal water.
questions.p: Niger Delta na low coastal area wey get plenty creeks and water, so e get mangrove swamp forest. Dis kain tree get stilt roots wey fit survive for salty water.

questions.q: The Jos Plateau in north-central Nigeria became economically important in the colonial and post-colonial period mainly because of large-scale commercial mining of which mineral?
questions.e: The Jos Plateau is well known across West Africa for its rich deposits of tin (and associated columbite), which attracted large mining activities from colonial times. This gave Jos the nickname 'Tin City'.
questions.p: Jos Plateau dey famous for tin mining (and columbite) since colonial time, na why dem dey call Jos 'Tin City'. Na dis mineral mining make di area important economically.

questions.q: The Jos Plateau is noticeably cooler than many surrounding lowland areas of Nigeria that share a similar latitude. What is the main reason for this cooler climate?
questions.e: Temperature generally falls as altitude increases. The Jos Plateau stands at a much higher elevation (over 1,200 metres in places) than the surrounding lowlands, so it experiences cooler temperatures even though it is far from the coast.
questions.p: As altitude dey increase, temperature dey reduce. Jos Plateau high pass di lowlands wey surround am (pass 1,200 metres for some places), na why e cold reach even though e no near sea.

questions.q: A geography teacher tells her class that Nigeria lies approximately between latitude 4 degrees North and latitude 14 degrees North. Based on this information, what is the approximate north-south latitudinal extent of the country?
questions.e: The latitudinal extent is found by subtracting the lower latitude from the higher one: 14°N minus 4°N equals 10°. This 10-degree spread explains why Nigeria has varied climate and vegetation from the coast to the far north.
questions.p: To find di extent, you go minus di smaller latitude from di bigger one: 14 take away 4 na 10°. Na dis 10 degree spread na im cause why Nigeria get different climate and vegetation from coast reach far north.

questions.q: The confluence town of Lokoja, where River Niger meets River Benue, is often used by geographers to explain Nigeria's regional divisions. Which statement best explains the geographical significance of this confluence point?
o: It is where River Niger and River Benue meet, forming a Y-shaped drainage pattern that divides the country into regions
It marks the boundary between forest and savanna only
It is the source of both River Niger and River Benue
It marks the southern coastline of Nigeria
questions.e: River Niger flows from the north-west and River Benue flows from the north-east, joining at Lokoja to form a Y-shape. This drainage pattern is commonly used to describe how the two rivers roughly separate Nigeria into northern and southern regions.
questions.p: River Niger dey come from north-west, River Benue dey come from north-east, dem go meet for Lokoja make Y-shape. Dis pattern na im dem dey use explain how di rivers dey roughly separate Nigeria into north and south regions.

questions.q: Which of the following states is NOT part of the Niger Delta region of Nigeria?
questions.e: Kano State is located in the far north of Nigeria, within the Sudan savanna region, far from the coastal, oil-producing Niger Delta. Bayelsa, Delta and Rivers States are all core Niger Delta states.
questions.p: Kano State dey far north, inside Sudan savanna area, e no near di coastal oil-producing Niger Delta. Bayelsa, Delta and Rivers na di main Niger Delta states.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of ECOWAS located?
questions.e: The ECOWAS Secretariat (Commission) is headquartered in Abuja, the capital of Nigeria. Accra, Lome and Dakar are important West African cities but none hosts the ECOWAS headquarters.
questions.p: ECOWAS main office dey Abuja, Nigeria capital. Accra, Lome and Dakar na big towns but no be where ECOWAS dey.

questions.q: Which treaty led to the formation of ECOWAS?
questions.e: The Treaty of Lagos, signed in 1975 by West African heads of state, created ECOWAS. The Treaty of Rome formed the European Economic Community, Versailles ended World War I issues, and the Treaty of Abuja (1991) later established the African Economic Community, not ECOWAS.
questions.p: Na Treaty of Lagos bring ECOWAS come for 1975. Treaty of Rome na for Europe, Versailles na for World War, and Abuja Treaty na for African Economic Community wey come later.

questions.q: Which of the following West African countries has no direct access to the sea (is landlocked)?
questions.e: Niger lies in the interior of West Africa and is surrounded by other countries with no coastline on the sea. Nigeria, Ghana and Senegal all border the Atlantic Ocean.
questions.p: Niger no get coastline, e dey inside land surrounded by other kontri. Nigeria, Ghana and Senegal all dey touch Atlantic Ocean.

questions.q: West Africa, as a region, is bounded in the south by the Atlantic Ocean and in the north by which major physical feature?
questions.e: West Africa's northern boundary merges into the Sahara Desert, which separates it from North Africa, while the Atlantic Ocean forms its southern and western limits. The Mediterranean, Indian Ocean and Red Sea are nowhere near West Africa.
questions.p: West Africa dey meet Sahara Desert for north side, and Atlantic Ocean dey for south. Mediterranean, Indian Ocean and Red Sea no near West Africa at all.

questions.q: The main objective behind the founding of ECOWAS was to:
o: promote economic cooperation and integration to raise the standard of living of member states
unite member states under one official religion
form a single political government for member states
establish a joint military command to fight external enemies
questions.e: ECOWAS was primarily set up for economic integration, such as free movement of goods, services and people, to improve living standards across West Africa. It was not created for political union, military command alone, or religious unity, although it later added security protocols.
questions.p: ECOWAS purpose na to help economy join together, make goods, people and services move free, so people life go better. E no be for one political government, military command or religion.

questions.q: A geography student travelling by road from the Guinea Coast of West Africa northward to the edge of the Sahara Desert will pass through vegetation belts in which correct order?
o: Rainforest, Mangrove swamp, Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna
Mangrove swamp, Rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
Guinea savanna, Rainforest, Mangrove swamp, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna, Rainforest, Mangrove swamp
questions.e: Moving from the coast inland and northward, rainfall decreases steadily, so vegetation changes from mangrove swamp near the coast, through rainforest, then Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, and finally Sahel savanna close to the Sahara. This order follows the decreasing rainfall gradient from south to north.
questions.p: As you dey waka comot coast go north, rain dey reduce small small, so vegetation go change from mangrove swamp, rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, reach Sahel savanna near Sahara. Na di rain amount dey arrange dis belts like dat.
